name: Forest Sauvage
summary: Albion's frontier wood between Camelot Hills and the Pennines: Castle Sauvage at its gate, Caer Renaris and the relic keep Castle Excalibur to the north, the fellwoods and Mist Hunters, and the Green Knight.

facts.text: Castle Sauvage, north-east of Camelot Hills, is an entrance to the Albion frontier.

Forest Sauvage is zone 11 of region 1, a frontier zone of about 430 monsters: fellwoods of many kinds, rainbow sprites, forest giants and ettins, forest hunters (faction Mist Hunters) under Rob Ria, death stalkers, adders, ancient basilisks and small skeletal legionnaires (Spirits of Rome).

facts.text: Castle Sauvage (area at 585085, 477504) holds Lord Mathius, Lieutenants Kuebler and Watson, Sir Benitt, Sir Tilian, Arly Camden, Caelin Finan, Scout Dherin, Sister Ellayne and the stable master Uliam.

facts.text: Albion's relics are named Merlin's Staff and the Scabbard of Excalibur; which keep holds which is not in the tables read (Castle Excalibur holding the Scabbard is inferred from the name, to verify).

The Green Knight (level 79, 100,000 health) stands at 592359, 418245 on the northern edge. His greeting: his forest is 'a delicate beast that can easily turn against you'; 'Tread lightly! I am ever watchful of my home!'
The weekly frontier quests of all three realms ask for the Green Knight, Evern and the Glacier Giant ('large monsters have blocked the supply lines in our frontier').

Quests: Kindred of the Fallen (Kuebler, Sir Tillian, Aiellana, two standing stones of power, a wounding stone, a summoned druid); Dugan's Magical Totem (the eyes of Brodecia at the ettin camp north-east of Castle Sauvage); Departed Fellowship (Cadwallen's sacrificial dagger and the hornbeam, silver oaken, gold oaken, knotted and gnarled fellwoods); The Forest Plot (Rob Ria's Mist Hunters).

story:
The wood at the edge. Forest Sauvage is the wild wood that lies between Camelot Hills and the high Pennines, and for as long as Albion has had a frontier this has been the first of it. The forest is older than the realm. The woodsmen of Castle Sauvage say it is not quite a forest: it is a beast lying down, the trees are its fur, the rivers its veins, and the deadwood in it is not dead, only asleep. They cut timber at its southern edge and nowhere else, and they cut it quietly.

The castle and the keeps. Castle Sauvage stands at the southern edge where the road comes up out of Camelot Hills, and it is the realm's front door: Lord Mathius holds it with his lieutenants, Kuebler and Watson, and Sir Benitt and Sir Tilian keep its upper rooms and send the young of the realm out into the wood on errands they come back from older. North through the forest, where the trees thin towards the hills, stand the two keeps of Sauvage: Caer Renaris in the west, a frontier hold of the old pattern, and Castle Excalibur to the east of it, one of the two keeps in Albion built to hold a relic of the realm. The riders say the Scabbard of Excalibur lies there, the scabbard whose wearer could not bleed, and that this is why the castle was named as it was; the enemy realms come through the northern passes year after year to take it. Between the keeps and the castle the forest belongs to nobody.

What lives in it. The fellwoods walk there, the deadwood that woke: ebony and ashen and hornbeam and black poplar, willow and aspen and oak, and in the north the knotted fellwoods that stand like old men by the Green Knight's road. Rainbow sprites crowd the western glades. Forest giants keep the eastern hills and ettins the north-east, with a camp on the south bank of the river under one Brodecia, whose eyes a carver of Caer Witrin wants for a totem. Death stalkers and adders and old basilisks haunt the ground round the castle, and among the trees halfway north small skeletons in Roman harness still march, legionaries of some cohort that went into the wood and was not relieved. In the east the Mist Hunters keep their own camps under Rob Ria, hunters of the old forest who answer to no lord. And at the northern edge of the forest, where the road climbs towards the Pennines, a knight in green stands among the trees.

The keeper. The Green Knight is courteous. He greets every traveller who stops to speak with him, and he warns them that his forest is a delicate beast that turns easily on those who mistreat it, and that if the beast is woken he must rise to defend it. He has never once drawn on anyone who did not ask him to; the woodsmen say a beast is woken by being asked. The bards of Camelot know a Green Knight from the old romance, who rode into Arthur's hall at Christmas and offered a game of one blow for one blow, a year apart, and was struck and picked up his own head. Whether this is the same knight nobody has asked him. Midgard and Hibernia have their own names for him and send their war-bands through the passes to hunt him, as Albion sends its own against their great beasts, because he stands where every road into Albion's frontier must go by him.

Why it matters to Albion. Sauvage is where the realm's wars begin and where its young are first sent to be tested. Every company that rides out to the keeps passes the castle, and the forest, and the knight. Lord Mathius keeps the castle and the keeps keep the relic; the Green Knight keeps the wood, and he keeps it for nobody's realm but its own.
legend: Forest Sauvage is Albion's frontier wood, levels teens to 30s, between Camelot Hills and the Pennines. Castle Sauvage in the south is the frontier gate: merchants, a healer, Lord Mathius, Lieutenant Kuebler (Kindred of the Fallen and a lot of courier quests), Sir Tilian upstairs, Arly Camden and Caelin Finan for Feast of the Decadent. North are the keeps: Caer Renaris and Castle Excalibur, the relic keep the other realms come for. The Green Knight (79, 100k) stands on the north edge of the wood. He is peaceful until someone whispers 'defend it' to him, so nobody pulls him by accident. He is a big one: bring a raid, melee does the work (he shrugs off most magic). Felwood rises at everyone's feet about every half minute, he goes for a healer every minute or so, his swings set off a heat burst around his target, and at every 10% he breaks off and walks to one of four spots nearby. Follow him and he only heals a sliver. Leave him for a minute and he is full again. Midgard and Hibernia have him on their weekly kill list too, so expect company. Rob Ria and the Mist Hunters are in the east; Brodecia's ettin camp is north-east on the river.

firstEntry: Forest Sauvage. Tread lightly. Something is watching.
The deadwood here is only asleep.
Albion's frontier begins under these trees.

An axe rings once to the south, then stops.

loremaster.intro: [Forest sauvage] is the wild wood at Albion's edge, and the woodsmen say it is a [beast] lying down. Ask of [castle sauvage], [caer renaris] and [castle excalibur]; of the [fellwoods] and the [gold oaken fellwood]; of [brodecia], the [fallen druid seer] and the [standing stones]; of the [mist hunters] and the [roman march]; or of the keeper of the wood, the [green knight].

topics.forest sauvage: The wild wood between Camelot Hills and the Pennines, the first of Albion's frontier. The woodsmen say it is a [beast] lying down. [Castle sauvage] keeps its southern edge, [caer renaris] and [castle excalibur] its northern, and the [green knight] keeps the wood itself.
topics.beast: The trees are its fur, the woodsmen say, the rivers its veins, and the deadwood is only asleep. The [green knight] tells every traveller himself: wake the beast within and he must rise to defend it. He waits to be asked.
topics.castle sauvage: Albion's frontier gate at the southern edge of [forest sauvage]. Lord Mathius holds it, with Lieutenants Kuebler and Watson; Sir Benitt and Sir Tilian keep the upper rooms and send the young out on errands. Every company that rides north to the keeps passes its gate.
topics.caer renaris: A frontier hold of the old pattern in the north-west of [forest sauvage]. A gold-barked [gold oaken fellwood] walks the trees below it.
topics.castle excalibur: One of Albion's two relic keeps, in the north of [forest sauvage]. The riders say the Scabbard of Excalibur is kept there, the scabbard whose wearer could not bleed; the realm's two relics are Merlin's Staff and the Scabbard. Midgard and Hibernia come through the northern passes for it.
topics.fellwoods: The deadwood of Sauvage that woke and walks: ebony, ashen, hornbeam, black poplar, willow, aspen, oak, and the knotted fellwoods by the [green knight]'s road. When he is roused, the rotting kind stand up at every traveller's feet.
topics.gold oaken fellwood: A fellwood with gold in its bark that walks below [caer renaris], older than the castle. The Church's champions hunt it with Cadwallen's sacrificial dagger from the druids' underground hall in Campacorentin, one of five fellwoods the dagger must taste before it will point the way to the ruined tower by Hadrian's Wall. The woodsmen call it the forest's purse and leave it be.
topics.brodecia: The ettin who heads the camp on the south bank of the river, north-east of [castle sauvage]. Dugan Advien, the wood carver of Caer Witrin, wants the eyes of Brodecia for a totem, and Brodecia, having two heads, has four of them and is careful with all four. The woodsmen say the camp moved there to watch the [mist hunters], and the hunters to watch the camp.
topics.fallen druid seer: A druid seer who fell among the [standing stones] east of the river in the old wars of the druids, and did not stay fallen. Sir Tilian of [castle sauvage] sends the young after her kin: a wounding stone set between the two stones, nearer the larger, calls one of the fallen up to be ended.
topics.standing stones: Two stones of power east of the river in [forest sauvage], the larger and the lesser, where the [fallen druid seer] walks. Aiellana of Adribard's Retreat knows what they were for and tells only those Sir Tilian sends her.
topics.mist hunters: The hunters of the old forest in the east of [forest sauvage], under [rob ria]. They answer to no lord of Camelot's and hunt only what the wood allows; they trade with those they have learned to trust.
topics.roman march: Small skeletons in Roman harness, legionaries and a centurion or two, still marching between the castle and the keeps: a cohort that went into the wood in the province's day and was not relieved.
topics.green knight: He stands by the road at the northern edge of [forest sauvage] and warns those who stop. He fights only those who ask him to defend his wood. Then the deadwood stands up at every man's feet, his sword sets the air alight round the struck man, he breaks off to walk between his clearings as he is wounded, and he goes past the front rank for whoever kneels over the hurt.

book.title: What the Woodsman Said
pages: What the Woodsman Said: the account of Old Hopcyn, woodcutter of Castle Sauvage forty years, as taken down by Lieutenant Kuebler's clerk because the lieutenant wanted it written before Hopcyn died, and Hopcyn wanted it written so that the lieutenant would stop asking. Go past him on the road and he will speak to you. He always does. He told me the forest was a delicate beast and that I was wise to stop and speak with him, and I thanked him and walked on with my axe over my shoulder and did not cut a single branch until I was out of sight of him.

I have cut wood in Sauvage forty years. I have never once cut it within sight of him. That is the whole of my secret, and I give it freely. The young ones from the castle do not believe it is so simple. He never draws on you unless you ask him to, I tell them. He tells you what will happen if the beast wakes, and then he waits, and it is you who has to say the word. A beast is woken by being asked. I have seen three men ask him in forty years. One of them came back.

The one who came back was a knight of the castle in his first summer, with a company behind him out of Camelot. He told me what he had seen while I mended his axe-handle, which he had broken on a felwood. The deadwood stood up everywhere at once, he said, a tree at every man's feet, so that a company of forty fought forty trees as well as the knight, and the more of them came, the more trees. He said the green man's sword set the air alight round whoever it struck, and the men at that man's shoulder burned with him.

He said the green man was not to be turned by words. The company's wizards threw everything they had and it ran off him like rain off holly, but the axes bit, and the swords. He said, and this is the part he told me twice, that the green man went past the knights in front of him every so often as if they were not there, to cut at whoever was kneeling over the wounded. The company lost two of its priests that way before they learned to keep a shield-wall round them that was not facing the knight at all.

And he said the green man would not stay where he was hurt. When the company had cut him a while he broke off and walked away from them, not fast, not fighting, through the trees to another clearing, and stood there and took a breath, and the green came back into him a little. Only a little. The company followed him every time and he never went to the same clearing twice running. There were four clearings, the knight thought, all within a long bowshot of the knotted trees. He drew me a map of them on the back of his muster roll. I burned it, and I told him why: a man who knows where the green man is going will follow him, and I have cut wood in Sauvage forty years by not following him.

Last, because the lieutenant asked. When a company gives up and leaves him, the knight told me, he stands where they left him a few breaths, and then he is whole again, every cut closed, and he bows to the empty road and walks back to his place by the knotted trees and the deadwood lies down. Then the next company comes, from our realm or from the other two, and stops, and he speaks to them as courteously as before. I asked the knight why he had gone back the second year. He said he wanted to see whether the green man remembered him. He did not come back.
